review_text: Cyberpunk 2077 is a very good story game and I recommend it to everyone. The game offers a huge variety of weapons and advanced technology, and the combat feels excellent and satisfying. The story is one of the strongest parts of the game, and your choices can affect how events unfold. At the beginning you create your character and choose their background, which slightly changes how some situations play out. The world is filled with interesting and crazy characters that make the experience even more memorable. I also highly recommend watching the anime Cyberpunk: Edgerunners before playing. It takes place about a year before the events of the game and adds more depth to the world. Overall: 10/10.

Of course I enjoyed CP2077, but I almost want to give it a negative rating to emphasize why I think it's merely a "really good" game as opposed to an "incredible" one. The storyline was a highlight (compelling and with choices that mattered), but there is very little mechanically in the game that hasn't been done before: GTA4/5 defined the standard for open worlds decades ago, and any mainline RPG has similar depth for character choices, skill trees, progression etc. So, does CP2077 differentiate with an immersive world that is truly novel? For me, not really. The map is expansive with some incredible artwork, but can feel samey within any given district. The characters, while memorable, are ultimately formulaic. The voice acting was surprisingly lacking in places (male V sounds like he's reading out instructions for a dishwasher). Towards the latter stages of the game, the combat starts to feel mundane due to a lack of enemy diversity. Despite playing with the latest patch (April 2026), the game is still super buggy: floating world items, stuttering animations, glitching quests, CTDs (all of which are perhaps to be expected for a game of this scale, but still no less annoying). I enjoyed my play-through, but don't see a reason to replay any time soon!

The story is the main driver of the game, with everything I make V say seems to matter in some way. It's refreshing to have an impact on the story, where there is no illusion of choice. Do you like big, open-world games and bleak, dystopian science fiction films? Do you like good storylines where decisions affect the outcomes? Do you like to spend a lot of time killing people and driving/racing many vehicles with very different handling characteristics? Are you into body modifications, nudity, sex scenes and extreme profanity? Do you want to lose weeks of your life in a deeply immersive environment that keeps bringing you back for more? If so, you've found the right game. Blending elements of Blade Runner, Mad Max (game and movies), Brazil, GTA, Fallout, Read Dead Redemption it is a visual treat from start to finish. You'll need a fairly decent PC if you want to have all the graphics settings maxed out but it's definitely worth it. The storylines are good and most of the main characters are well-developed and interesting enough to make you care about their survival. There were a few minor glitches evident in my first play through (e.g. candles burning under water and cops spawning out of thin air) but most seem to have been fixed in subsequent patches. The Phantom Liberty expansion adds a few hours of gameplay and more variety to the storytelling and is a worthy addition to the main game. Explore vast areas and experience many different settings, each with their own clans and vibes. Gameplay varies from relaxed and serene to full on madness, so there's something for everyone. Well, not everyone. With sex, nudity, violence, drugs and a lot of very strong language, this is a game best played when there are no young kids around. If you value your job and/or family time, you may want to set the alarm on your phone to drag you back into the real world every now and then. I played this on a Windows PC using an Xbox controller and that worked fine, although the controls could sometimes be a little fiddly. I have completed it twice, exploring different storylines and experiencing two very different endings. After 188 hours in the game I'm ready to play something else for while, but I will revisit this in the future. It's absolutely brilliant and highly addictive. 9/10. It lost a point for the occasionally frustrating controls.

Despite all the crap I am going to say about it- I simply love this game. This game is throughout quite an immersive and fun experience, that is ocasionally ruined a little bit with the hicups caused by some tedious issues. The story, while it explores tropes that are typical to this genre - it does it quite well. Colorful (maybe too much during daytime) yet dark, near altfuture, urban dystopia. Society indulged, obsessed and drained both with consumerism and sex. Uploading the very soul to the net. Exploring the topics of afterlife, leaving a mark in the world, identity and fighting with the system. Characters are well written, they fit in perfectly and so does the dialogue. There is a lot of memorable quests and peeps, especially among the main cast. I love both Johnny's and V's characters, their relationship and how they interact with eachother. Kudos to English female V voice actress, her performance was amazing. Graphically it is stunning. The lights, effects, sounds, atmosphere, weapons, buildings and especially car models - all of this builds up the world almost flawlessly. Night City does look and feel authentic. The music is spot on, both in the game's soundtrack and it's radio track selection - they literally did a 10/10 job here, especially with the Samurai bits. But... Sadly this whole immersive experience can be broken by the bugs that persisted in this game over the years. You can spot civilians phasing through walls, multiple car models being stuck on top of or inside each other, enemies shooting you through some walls, animations/scripted events not playing correctly or at all. One of the more annoying bugs that I remember from when I first played the game ~5 years ago was "clown boots" - the game loops the sound of the crushing bottles as your footsteps when you first walk on them in specific area during the Evelyn questline and it doesn't stop unless you restart the game... Luckily I didn't run into anything that was game breaking or soft locking my progress. The game also flatlined like two times for me. Yet it is still disappointing seeing that those old issues weren't fixed, despite devs supporting the game and pushing new updates over the years. Bugs are very rare, yet they are there. It also feels that the further you go from the start of the game, there is less of them. AI could also be better as it is very basic. Civilian behaviour feels mostly like an "A" than an "I". On top of everything the police is not a threat at all. You can lose a tail in mere seconds and it feels like they are not even interested in chasing you. Whats also a bit wild is that pedestrians tend to jump under your wheels for no reason, as if they were trying to avoid your vehicle... in the wrong direction.., even if you were not a threat to them to begin with. And then, there is a Sinnerman quest - an absolute joke... I would still strongly recommend getting this game. It's not without its flaws, but it is truly a great experience. It also does hold a replayability value with the build variety, some choices you make during the story and it has a mod support. Just keep in mind that you will eventually encounter bugs that will make the world of the game less believable to you. Would bomb Saka tower again tho.

It's a good game, but not a good RPG. However I'd say the same for CDPR's other games, so if you enjoyed Witcher 3, the mechanical depth and amount of choices/roleplaying opportunities should satisfy you. In terms of structure and gameplay, I'd compare it more to Grand Theft Auto than anything else. Writing is solid, and the acting is especially great. The story is dramatic and memorable, but it isn't particularly deep. Don't go in expecting it to dive into the philosophy of the cyberpunk genre, or expand on its themes very much. The atmosphere is pretty incredible though, nothing beats driving through Night City in the rain, blasting Refused on the in-game radio. Combat is fun, there's a lot to think about due to the quick hacks, and there's a good amount of weapon variety as well. Feels great on both mouse/keyboard and controller. Overall an above average game. I enjoyed it.

I bought Cyberpunk at launch. It was an unfinished nightmare of bugs, unbalanced gameplay, and horrific instability. I was pretty sure I'd hate it forever but after coming back to it last year and beating it twice it's both one of the best fps games ever made and one of the best open world games ever made. The world feels densely packed like Sleeping Dogs while having the scope of something like Red Dead or Ghosts of Tsushima. The universe is absurdly well thought out and brought to life so vividly its hard to believe this is the mess I played years ago. Side quests are divided into jobs and gigs and while the gigs feel like a relic of late 2000s/early 2010s open world games the side jobs are almost all phenomenal and have a cinematic feel that many main stories in other games don't have. Gunplay and melee combat are snappy and satisfying, hacking is a blast and elevates fights in such a fun way, the driving isn't great but it's good enough I can play with a mouse and keyboard without wanting to grab a controller and through my PC through a wall. It's made better by the fact that there's some really fun vehicles, especially for people who are fans of the movies this is influenced by (yes of course I want to park the Akira bike next to the Blade Runner noodle shop). CD Projekt Red deserves all the grief they got for this game at launch but I've loved the story, characters, world, and gameplay that Cyberpunk has become now that it's. You know. A finished game.

Everything is amazing, from the story, the graphics, the gore, the alive city.
